extracted.intended_audience: national competent authorities, IP offices, WIPO staff, legal practitioners and beneficiaries involved in international registration and protection of appellations of origin and geographical indications
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and standards for applying for, registering, protecting, refusing, amending and administering international registrations of appellations of origin and geographical indications under the Geneva Act of the Lisbon Agreement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions / Abbreviated expressions (Article 1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Defines key terms used throughout the Act, including: 'Lisbon Agreement', '1967 Act', 'this Act', 'Regulations', 'Paris Convention', 'appellation of origin', 'geographical indication', 'International Register', 'international registration', 'application', 'registered', 'geographical area of origin', 'trans-border geographical area', 'Contracting Party', 'Contracting Party of Origin', 'Competent Authority', 'beneficiaries', 'intergovernmental organization', 'Organization' (WIPO), 'Director General', and 'International Bureau'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These definitions set the scope and meaning of subsequent provisions (e.g., what constitutes an appellation of origin vs a geographical indication; how 'registered' and 'International Register' are used).

rubrics_metrics.name: Subject-matter of protection (Article 2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Protects: (i) denominations containing or consisting of the name of a geographical area serving to designate a good as originating there, where quality/characteristics are due exclusively or essentially to the geographical environment (natural and human factors) and have given the good its reputation (appellation of origin); and (ii) indications identifying a good as originating in a geographical area where a given quality, reputation or other characteristic is essentially attributable to geographical origin (geographical indication).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also specifies that a geographical area of origin may be entire territory, region, locality, place, or trans-border area; this is the substantive eligibility test for registrations under the Act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designation of Competent Authority (Article 3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each Contracting Party must designate an entity responsible for administration of the Act in its territory and communications with the International Bureau, and notify the International Bureau of the name and contact details as specified in the Regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a mandatory procedural requirement for filing/communications; failure to designate or notify may affect filings and notifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: International Register maintenance (Article 4)
rubrics_metrics.description: The International Bureau shall maintain an International Register recording international registrations effected under this Act, under the Lisbon Agreement and the 1967 Act, and related data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Register is the official collection of data concerning international registrations, regardless of medium; it is the authoritative record for dates, publications, refusals, withdrawals, etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Place of filing (Article 5(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications shall be filed with the International Bureau.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing channel is centralized: filings go to the International Bureau unless domestic/Regulations provide otherwise (e.g., declarations permitting direct filing).

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may file an application (Article 5(2)–(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: Subject to Article 5(3), the Competent Authority files the application in the name of (i) the beneficiaries; or (ii) a natural person or legal entity having legal standing under the law of the Contracting Party of Origin to assert the beneficiaries' rights. If the legislation of the Contracting Party of Origin permits, beneficiaries or an authorized person may file directly (subject to a declaration).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing by beneficiaries directly requires a declaration by the Contracting Party; filings by Competent Authorities are the default route. The page details timing/effect of such declarations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Joint application for trans‑border geographical areas (Article 5(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: For trans-border geographical areas, adjacent Contracting Parties may, by agreement, file an application jointly through a commonly designated Competent Authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permits cooperative filings for geographical indications that cover territories in more than one Contracting Party of Origin.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory and optional contents of application (Article 5(5)–(6))
rubrics_metrics.description: The Regulations shall specify the mandatory particulars to be included in the application (in addition to those in Article 6(3)) and may specify optional particulars.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Substantive and formal particulars required for application completeness are delegated to the Regulations; applicants must follow Regulations for particulars to avoid delays or altered registration dates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formal examination and registration by the International Bureau (Article 6(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon receipt of an application in due form (as specified in the Regulations), the International Bureau shall register the appellation of origin or geographical indication in the International Register.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registration is subject to formal examination under the Regulations; substantive examination by Contracting Parties occurs through refusal procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Date of international registration and effect of missing particulars (Article 6(2) and (3))
rubrics_metrics.description: The date of international registration is the date the application was received by the International Bureau, except where required particulars are missing (identification of Competent Authority/applicant, beneficiaries, appellation/indication, or goods): in that case the date is the date on which the last missing particular is received.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Completeness affects the official registration date, which in turn affects the date from which protection may be claimed and time limits for refusal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication and notification of international registrations (Article 6(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: The International Bureau shall, without delay, publish each international registration and notify the Competent Authority of each Contracting Party of the international registration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publication triggers the opportunity for Contracting Parties to consider protection and to communicate refusals within applicable time limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Date of effect of international registration (Article 6(5))
rubrics_metrics.description: A registered appellation or geographical indication shall be protected, in each Contracting Party that has not refused protection or that has sent a notification of grant of protection, from the date of the international registration, subject to the possibility for a Contracting Party to declare a different protection start date (not later than the expiry of the time limit for refusal in the Regulations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contracting Parties may make declarations setting an alternate effective date in accordance with national/regional law; however such date cannot be later than the denial/refusal time limit set in the Regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fees for registration and other entries (Article 7)
rubrics_metrics.description: International registration of each appellation/geographical indication is subject to the fee specified in the Regulations; the Regulations specify fees for other entries and information; reduced fees may be established (particularly for developing/least-developed countries).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Assembly fixes fee amounts; fee reductions and special arrangements are possible. Non-payment of an individual fee required by a Contracting Party (for substantive examination) results (per Regulations) in renunciation of protection in that Contracting Party.

rubrics_metrics.name: Individual fee and administrative fees (Article 7(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: Any Contracting Party may declare that protection extends to it only if a fee is paid to cover its cost of substantive examination; the amount must not exceed the equivalent of the national fee diminished by savings from the international procedure. The Contracting Party may also require an administrative fee relating to beneficiaries' use. Non-payment of such an individual fee may effect renunciation for that Contracting Party.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This permits Contracting Parties to recoup domestic examination costs, subject to limits; applicants should check declarations to know where protection requires additional payment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Period of validity and dependency on protection in Contracting Party of Origin (Article 8(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: International registrations are valid indefinitely, on the understanding that protection ceases if the denomination/indication is no longer protected in the Contracting Party of Origin.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintaining domestic protection in the Contracting Party of Origin is a precondition for continued international protection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cancellation of international registration (Article 8(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: The Competent Authority of the Contracting Party of Origin or, where applicable, beneficiaries or authorized persons, may request cancellation of the international registration at any time. If the denomination/indication is no longer protected in the Contracting Party of Origin, the Competent Authority shall request cancellation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cancellation can be initiated by origin authorities or beneficiaries, and occurs mandatorily where domestic protection lapses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commitment to protect by Contracting Parties (Article 9)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each Contracting Party shall protect registered appellations of origin and geographical indications on its territory within its own legal system and practice but in accordance with the terms of this Act, subject to refusals, renunciations, invalidations or cancellations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parties that do not distinguish between appellations of origin and geographical indications domestically are not required to introduce such a distinction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form of legal protection and relation to other instruments (Article 10)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each Contracting Party is free to choose the type of legislation under which it establishes the protection provided by the Act, provided such legislation meets the substantive requirements; the Act does not affect other protection a Party may accord under national/regional law or other international instruments, nor derogate from obligations under other instruments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Domestic implementation may vary (e.g., sui generis GI law, trademark law, unfair competition), but must satisfy the Act's substantive protection obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content of protection – prohibitions and scope (Article 11(1)–(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties shall provide legal means to prevent: (a)(i) use of the appellation/indication in respect of goods of the same kind not originating in the geographical area or not complying with requirements for use; (a)(ii) use in respect of goods not of the same kind or services if such use indicates or suggests a connection and would likely damage beneficiaries' interests or unfairly impair/dilute or take advantage of reputation; and (b) any other practice liable to mislead consumers as to origin, provenance or nature of goods. Protection also applies to imitation (even if true origin indicated), translations, and uses accompanied by words such as 'style', 'kind', 'type', 'imitation' etc. Contracting Party shall refuse or invalidate a later trademark if its use would result in situations covered by paragraph (1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Broad substantive protection covering both direct misrepresentation and unfair exploitation or dilution of reputation; Parties must provide trademark refusal/invalidation where appropriate, ex officio if domestic law permits or at request of interested party.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protection against becoming generic (Article 12)
rubrics_metrics.description: Registered appellations of origin and geographical indications cannot be considered to have become generic in a Contracting Party, subject to the agreed statement that elements with a generic character in the Contracting Party of Origin need not be protected in other Contracting Parties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Act preserves GI status against genericide claims across Contracting Parties, but recognizes existing generic elements and prior use exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Safeguards concerning other rights (Article 13)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Act does not prejudice prior trademarks applied for or registered in good faith or acquired through use in good faith; where domestic law provides limited exceptions to trademark rights, such exceptions apply. The Act also does not prejudice the right to use personal names in business, or plant variety/animal breed denominations, except where such use would mislead the public. If a Contracting Party withdraws a refusal or grants protection after earlier finding prior rights, the resulting protection shall not prejudice that prior right unless the prior right has been cancelled/non-renewed/revoked/invalidated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balancing GI protection with pre-existing trademark and other rights: prior rights in good faith are preserved; notifications of grant/withdrawal must account for such rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enforcement procedures and remedies (Article 14)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each Contracting Party shall make available effective legal remedies for protection of registered appellations and geographical indications and provide that legal proceedings may be brought by a public authority or any interested party (natural or legal, public or private), depending on its legal system and practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parties must ensure enforceability through appropriate civil/criminal/administrative remedies; standing may be broad (public authorities or interested parties).

rubrics_metrics.name: Refusal of effects of international registration (Article 15)
rubrics_metrics.description: Within the time limit specified in the Regulations, the Competent Authority of a Contracting Party may notify the International Bureau of refusal of the effects of an international registration in its territory, ex officio (if domestic law permits) or at the request of an interested party. The notification must set out the grounds for refusal. The International Bureau shall record, publish and communicate refusals and grounds. Parties must provide reasonable opportunity for anyone whose interests would be affected to request the Competent Authority to notify a refusal. Interested parties affected by a refusal shall have the same judicial and administrative remedies as nationals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refusal is the mechanism for substantive national examination and denial of protection; notifications must be timely and reasoned; procedural safeguards (opportunity to request refusal; remedies) are required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal of refusal (Article 16)
rubrics_metrics.description: A refusal may be withdrawn in accordance with procedures specified in the Regulations; a withdrawal shall be recorded in the International Register.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Withdrawal reverses the effect of an earlier refusal and is formally recorded and published by the International Bureau.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transitional period for terminating prior uses (Article 17)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a Contracting Party has not refused effects on ground of prior use by a third party, or has withdrawn such refusal or has notified a grant of protection, it may, if its legislation permits, grant a defined period (as specified in the Regulations) for terminating such prior use. The Contracting Party shall notify the International Bureau of any such period per Regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permits national law to grant incumbent users a limited transitional period to cease uses that conflict with newly protected GIs, with notification to the International Bureau.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification of grant of protection (Article 18)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Competent Authority of a Contracting Party may notify the International Bureau of the grant of protection to a registered appellation or geographical indication; the International Bureau shall record and publish such notification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formal mechanism to record that a Contracting Party has granted protection (as opposed to remaining silent or refusing).

rubrics_metrics.name: Invalidation of effects in Contracting Party (Article 19)
rubrics_metrics.description: Invalidation of effects (in whole or in part) of an international registration in the territory of a Contracting Party may be pronounced only after giving beneficiaries an opportunity to defend their rights (and the natural person or legal entity under Article 5(2)(ii)). The Contracting Party shall notify the invalidation to the International Bureau, which shall record and publish it. Invalidation shall not prejudice other protection that may be available under Article 10(2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedure safeguards (right to be heard) and recording/publication obligations apply; invalidation does not erase other available protections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedures for modifications and other entries in the International Register (Article 20)
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures for modification of international registrations and other entries in the International Register shall be specified in the Regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Changes to registrations (e.g., amendments, renewals, address changes) are governed by the Regulations; consult Regulations for procedural details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Membership of the Special Union (Article 21)
rubrics_metrics.description: Contracting Parties shall be members of the same Special Union as the States party to the Lisbon Agreement or the 1967 Act, whether or not they are party to the Lisbon Agreement or the 1967 Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutional alignment with the existing Lisbon/1967 special union is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assembly of the Special Union — composition, tasks, quorum and decision-making (Article 22)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each Contracting Party is represented by one delegate (with alternates/advisors/experts). The Assembly deals with maintenance/development of the Special Union and implementation of the Act; gives directions to the Director General; amends Regulations; reviews reports; determines program and budget; adopts financial regulations; establishes committees; determines observers; adopts certain amendments to Articles 22–24 and 27; and other functions. Quorum, decision-making seeks consensus but allows voting where needed (each State one vote; intergovernmental organizations may vote in place of member States under conditions). Decisions generally require two-thirds of votes cast (subject to exceptions). The Assembly meets ordinarily at same time/place as WIPO General Assembly and may meet extraordinarily; rules of procedure adopted by Assembly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This article sets the governance, procedural and voting rules for collective decision-making, amendment of Regulations, financial oversight and other institutional matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: International Bureau functions and Director General (Article 23)
rubrics_metrics.description: International Bureau performs international registration and related administrative duties, prepares meetings and provides Secretariat to the Assembly and committees. The Director General is Chief Executive of the Special Union, represents it, and (with staff) participates in meetings without vote and acts as ex officio Secretary. The Bureau prepares revision conferences and may consult with organizations; carries out other tasks assigned in relation to the Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes administrative/secretariat roles and non-voting participation of Director General/staff in Assembly and revision processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Finances — budget, sources, fee fixing, working capital and auditing (Article 24)
rubrics_metrics.description: Income/expenses of the Special Union reflected in WIPO budget. Income derived from: (i) fees under Article 7; (ii) proceeds from publications; (iii) gifts/bequests/subventions; (iv) rent/investment/miscellaneous income; (v) special contributions if other sources insufficient. Assembly fixes amounts of fees on proposal of Director General to cover expenses. Working capital fund may be constituted by advances by members; host State may grant advances if fund insufficient; auditing by member States or external auditors as provided in Financial Regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes financial framework and fee-setting responsibility (Assembly), including special contributions and contingencies for working capital and audits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulations — subject-matter, amendment thresholds and conflict rule (Article 25)
rubrics_metrics.description: Details for carrying out the Act are established in the Regulations. The Assembly may decide certain provisions of the Regulations may be amended only by unanimity or by three-fourths majority. In case of conflict between this Act and the Regulations, the Act prevails.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulations implement procedural particulars; the Assembly can set higher amendment thresholds for specific Regulations provisions; Regulations cannot override the Act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revision and amendment procedures (Articles 26–27)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Act may be revised by Diplomatic Conferences decided by the Assembly. Articles 22–24 and 27 may be amended either by revision conference or by the Assembly. Proposals for amendment of those Articles may be initiated by any Contracting Party or Director General and must be communicated six months in advance. Adoption requires specified majorities (generally three-fourths; some amendments require four-fifths). Entry into force rules for amendments are specified (notifications of acceptance by specified proportion, with exceptions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies procedural safeguards, advance notice, and qualified-majority thresholds for institutional amendments; consult the detailed majority/entry-into-force rules in Article 27.

rubrics_metrics.name: Becoming party — eligibility, ratification/accession and effective date (Article 28–29)
rubrics_metrics.description: Eligibility: States party to Paris Convention may sign/become party; other WIPO member States may become party if they declare legislative compliance with Paris Convention provisions; intergovernmental organizations may become party under conditions. States/organizations may deposit instrument of ratification (if signed) or accession (if not). Effective date of deposit generally the date of deposit. The Act enters into force three months after five eligible parties deposit instruments. Entry into force for subsequent depositors is three months after deposit or on later date indicated. Provisions apply to international registrations effected prior to accession (with applicable transitional procedures). No reservations permitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets eligibility criteria and temporal rules for entry into force and treatment of previously effected registrations; applicants and authorities must track effective dates and declarations attached to accessions/ratifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition of reservations (Article 30)
rubrics_metrics.description: No reservations to this Act are permitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contracting Parties cannot enter the Act subject to reservations; they must accept the Act as a whole.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relations with Lisbon Agreement and 1967 Act (Article 31)
rubrics_metrics.description: This Act alone applies between States party to both this Act and the Lisbon Agreement or the 1967 Act; States shall not accord lower protection with regard to international registrations effective under the Lisbon Agreement or the 1967 Act. States party to both this Act and Lisbon/1967 shall continue to apply the Lisbon Agreement/1967 Act in relations with States party to those instruments but not to this Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures continuity and non-reduction of protection for registrations under earlier instruments and clarifies applicable instrument depending on Parties' treaty status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Denunciation (Article 32)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any Contracting Party may denounce the Act by notification to the Director General. Denunciation takes effect one year after receipt (or later date indicated). Denunciation does not affect pending applications or international registrations in force in respect of the denouncing Party at the time denunciation comes into effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides exit mechanism while protecting existing registrations and pending processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Languages, signature and depositary (Article 33–34)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Act shall be signed in a single original in English, Arabic, Chinese, French, Russian and Spanish — all texts equally authentic. Official texts in other languages may be established by the Director General after consultation. The Act remains open for signature at WIPO headquarters for one year after adoption. The Director General is the depositary of the Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identifies authoritative language texts and depositary role for instruments and notifications.
